findings.title: Float rounding admits source durations that are not integral milliseconds
findings.contract: The closed first slice and diagnostic catalog require positive, finite, representable integral milliseconds. The reviewed plan requires nonrepresentable durations to reject. Decimal spelling must not silently acquire an integral interpretation after rounding.
findings.problem: DurationLiteral::milliseconds first parses the authored decimal into f64 and multiplies it by the unit factor, then tests fract()==0 and the safe-integer bound. The source's fractional information can already have been rounded away by that point. The job checker treats Some(ms) as validation and audit/CheckedJobBinding record the rounded integer.

reproductions.expected: TYPE_JOB_INTERVAL_INVALID: source is a nonintegral millisecond value
TYPE_JOB_INTERVAL_INVALID: exact source value is less than one millisecond and nonintegral
TYPE_JOB_INTERVAL_INVALID: exact source value is greater than one millisecond and nonintegral

findings.impact: The new public job frontend accepts values outside its closed interval contract and emits a checked static interval different from the authored value. Target remains nonexecuting, so no worker dispatch or scheduling effect was observed or implied.
findings.requiredChange: Validate duration scaling and integrality from the exact decimal spelling using checked integer/decimal arithmetic, or reject precision that cannot be validated without loss. Do not use rounded f64 as proof that the original duration is an integral supported interval. Preserve valid fractional-unit spellings such as 0.001s.
findings.requiredRegression: Add the three boundary spellings as rejected job intervals alongside valid exact fractional units, safe-integer edge, zero/negative and unsupported-unit cases; verify audit never publishes a rounded replacement for an invalid source interval.
findings.recheck: Run focused job tests and exact CLI/audit probes, then scoped independent correction review. No implementation fix was made by reviewer.

assessments.result: JobDeclaration carries name, DurationLiteral, invocation and closed enum clauses with source ranges. Contextual top-level dispatch rejects public jobs. Missing, duplicate, invalid and unknown clauses reject; invalid-first/valid-second clauses cannot remove earlier diagnostics. Nested unknown payload clauses reject. Cron and unsupported modes remain unsupported.

Ordinary zero, negative, submillisecond, unsupported-unit and out-of-range groups pass their rejection checks. Exact-decimal rounding loophole above remains a blocker; ordinary passing interval tests do not close it.

Exact authored callee is required as NodeKind::Action. Parameter must be one nonnullable named type directly refining Instant with no constraints, secret classification or generic arguments; result is exact builtin Unit. Only same-type explicit constructor with one intrinsic clock.now argument qualifies. Dedicated job clock environment invokes ordinary inference before recording CheckedJobBinding proof. Primitive ban is unchanged. Raw clock, nullable/constrained/indirect wrapper, generic parameter, unknown constructor owner, forged callee owner, nested arbitrary calls and extra principal inputs reject.

Jobs have separate NodeKind::Job entries and are not ordinary callables. Job-origin call resolution is exact, without receiver/suffix fallback. Constructors are visited for visibility/resolution while type construction does not create a callable edge. Corrected dedicated test proves job-to-action-to-provider reachability and approval reachability inclusion. Evidence is labelled static may-call, not execution or authority.

JobFailureSet is separate from callable and route sets and copies the checked action contract/may_suspend status. The unconstrained direct nominal Instant constructor records a no-additional-rejection proof. Durable dispositions remain pending_checked_worker_binding; no HTTP route mapping or retry budget is inferred from next_schedule.

Lower snake case, duplicate identity and non-callable use groups pass. Independent two-file CLI probes require both public action and type imports, reject missing imports and private action/type imports. Qualified entity action positive and forged receiver negatives pass existing focused groups. No job export is introduced.

audit/jobs.json is conditional on jobs; a no-jobs project emits no job artifact. The canonical job audit records exact action/snapshot constructor, 900000ms, reachable names, constructor proof, static effects label, null execution profile and runtime_lowering_supported:false. It currently rounds the invalid interval cases as reported. Corrected service audit group proves external effect and approval reachability without worker-conformance claims.

TargetGenerator returns JADPO_TARGET_JOB_NOT_IMPLEMENTED when collecting any Job before app target generation. Independent CLI build probes fail for valid and rounded interval cases, and no build/target/app.ts appears. Neither no-op registry nor startup execution is emitted.

Formatter group proves idempotence and preserved typed meaning; fixture 173 and its formatter snapshot have identical bytes. CLI LSP probe resolves run action to its declaration, constructor to its type declaration, returns three nominal-type reference occurrences and includes the job symbol. Dedicated job parser/type/target diagnostic catalog entries explain the closed contract and pending execution limits.

Frozen ASYNC document and trace catalog, SERVICE document and provider snapshot pins match the prior reviews. No worker/scheduler/auth/role/schema/event/public host execution was added or approved by this frontend review. Whole RM306, event binding, 18-trace conformance and reminder admission/runtime lowering remain pending.
